items.text: Opening description of the wood arrangement
items.text_en: Opening description of the wood arrangement
items.desc_en: This segment describes how the logs were tied with a rope made of palm fiber that had been soaked in seed, and where they were buried in the sandbank of the sea, noting that the wood produced a beam but no fruit, and that three of the four beams could not support a camel.

sub.desc_en: The Tanna describes how the logs were tied with a rope of palm fiber soaked in seed, buried in the sea's sandbank, producing a beam but no fruit, and that three of the four beams could not support a camel.

items.text: Debate on the reason for the gap between logs
items.text_en: Debate on the reason for the gap between logs
items.desc_en: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda dispute the purpose of the space between the logs: one says it allows the wind to fan the fire, the other says it allows the priests to kindle the flame from there. A challenge is raised from the Mishnah that explicitly states the space was for kindling, and the Gemara answers that different locations had different practices.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara asks what is the reason for the space between the logs in the arrangement.
Rav Huna and Rav Chisda dispute the purpose: one says it allows the wind to fan the fire, the other says it allows the priests to kindle the flame from there.
An objection is raised from the Mishnah that explicitly states the space was for kindling, contradicting the first opinion.
The Gemara resolves that different locations had different practices, so both opinions can be valid.

items.text: Transition to the Mishnah of the lottery
items.text_en: Transition to the Mishnah of the lottery
items.desc_en: This segment marks the return to the Mishnah 'Ra'uhu echav' and the beginning of the description of the daily lottery for the priestly duties.

sub.desc_en: The Gemara signals a return to the Mishnah 'Ra'uhu echav' and the start of the lottery procedure.

items.text: The lottery for the priestly duties
items.text_en: The lottery for the priestly duties
items.desc_en: The appointed officer calls for the priests to draw lots for who will perform the various services: slaughter, sprinkling, cleaning the inner altar and menorah, and bringing up the limbs. The list of the specific limbs and offerings is given, and the lot is cast, with the winner being the one who wins.

sub.desc_en: The appointed officer calls the priests to draw lots for who will perform the services of slaughter, sprinkling, cleaning the inner altar and menorah, and bringing up the limbs.

The Mishnah lists the specific limbs and offerings that are brought up: the head and right hind leg, the two forelegs, the tail and left hind leg, the breast and neck, the two flanks, the innards, the fine flour, the griddle-cake offering, and the wine.
The priests cast the lot, and the one who won performed the service.

items.text: The signal for the time of slaughter
items.text_en: The signal for the time of slaughter
items.desc_en: The officer tells the priests to go and see if the time for slaughter has arrived. If it has, the one who sees says 'Barkai'. Matya ben Shmuel says that the light of the entire east is visible until it is in Hebron, and the priest responds 'Hen'.

sub.desc_en: The Tanna reports that the officer tells the priests to go check if the time for slaughter has arrived, and the one who sees the signal says 'Barkai'.
Matya ben Shmuel says that the light of the entire east is visible until it reaches Hebron, describing the extent of the dawn signal.
The Tanna concludes that the priest responds 'Hen' (yes) to confirm the signal.

items.text: Bringing the lamb and the location of the chambers
items.text_en: Bringing the lamb and the location of the chambers
items.desc_en: The officer instructs to bring a lamb from the chamber of lambs, which is located in the northwestern corner. There are four chambers: one for lambs, one for seals, one for the fire room, and one for making the showbread. They then enter the chamber of vessels and bring out 93 silver and gold vessels, and water the Tamid with a cup.

sub.desc_en: The officer commands to bring a lamb from the chamber of lambs, located in the northwestern corner, and lists the four chambers there.
They enter the chamber of vessels, bring out 93 silver and gold vessels, and water the Tamid with a cup.

items.desc_en: The mishnah describes that the priest does not break the leg but pierces it through the heel and hangs it.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah states that the priest does not break the leg but pierces it through the heel and hangs it.

items.text: Flaying and cutting the head and legs
items.text_en: Flaying and cutting the head and legs
items.desc_en: The priest flays down to the chest, cuts off the head and gives it to the one who merited it, then cuts the legs and gives them, and removes the heart's blood.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah describes the priest flaying the offering down to the chest, cutting off the head and legs, and removing the heart's blood.

items.text: Cutting the forelegs and right hind leg
items.text_en: Cutting the forelegs and right hind leg
items.desc_en: The priest cuts the forelegs and gives them, then cuts the right hind leg with its two testicles, and tears the animal open to reveal everything.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah states that the priest cuts the forelegs and gives them to the one who won them.
The Mishnah continues that the priest goes up to the right hind leg, cuts it, and gives it with its two testicles to the one who won it.
The Mishnah concludes that the priest tears the animal open, revealing everything before him.

items.desc_en: The priest takes the fat and places it on the slaughter site of the head, then gives the entrails to be washed; the stomach is washed in the washing chamber, and the entrails are washed three times on marble tables.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah describes the priest taking the fat and placing it on the slaughter site of the head.
The Mishnah states that the priest takes the entrails and gives them to the one who won them to wash.
The Mishnah specifies that the stomach is washed in the washing chamber.
The Mishnah concludes that the stomach is washed thoroughly and the entrails are washed three times on marble tables between the pillars.

items.desc_en: The priest takes the knife, separates the lung from the liver and the lobe of the liver without moving it, then pierces the chest and gives it.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah describes the priest taking the knife and separating the lung from the liver and the lobe of the liver.
The Mishnah notes that the priest did not move the lung from its place.
The Mishnah concludes that the priest pierces the chest and gives the organ to the one who merited it.

items.desc_en: The priest cuts down the right flank to the spine without touching it until reaching between two thin ribs, then cuts it and gives it with the liver hanging from it.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah describes the procedure for cutting the right flank: the priest cuts downward to the spine without touching it, reaches between two thin ribs, cuts the flank, and gives it with the liver hanging from it.

items.desc_en: The priest comes to the neck, leaves two ribs on each side, cuts it, and gives it with the windpipe, heart, and lung hanging from it.

sub.desc_en: The Mishnah describes the priest approaching the neck (גרה), leaving two ribs on each side, cutting it, and handing it to the priest who won it, with the trachea (קנה), heart, and lung hanging from it.

items.text: Cutting the left flank and tail, and final distribution
items.text_en: Cutting the left flank and tail, and final distribution
items.desc_en: The priest cuts the left flank with two thin ribs above and below, then cuts it with the spine and spleen; he then cuts the tail with the fat tail, liver lobe, and two kidneys, and finally the left hind leg. All stand in a row with the limbs.

sub.desc_en: The mishnah describes how the priest approaches the left flank, leaving two thin ribs above and two below, just as he did for the right flank.
The mishnah explains that the left flank is cut and given to the priest who won it, along with the spine and spleen, and notes that the right flank is called 'large' because the liver hangs from it.
The mishnah describes cutting the tail and giving it to the winning priest, along with the fat tail, liver lobe, and two kidneys.
The mishnah concludes that the priest takes the left hind leg, cuts it, and gives it to the winning priest, and all the priests stand in a row with the limbs in their hands.
